source: Original Case002 15 hero scenes and canonical 89-node storyboard; four independently approved hero-gap image candidates HJ01, HF01, HE01 and HV01, with three final hero artworks pending.

scenes.focus: a broad-shouldered private detective in a rain-dark overcoat stands with his back to the viewer in a tense quiet exchange with a weary mustached private railway watchman who lowers his eyes instead of challenging him
scenes.camera: intimate vertical over-the-shoulder view from behind the detective on the right; watchman under the oil lantern on the left and the wet rail siding and lock gate receding in the fog
scenes.location: an old canal lock beside the private industrial railway siding and a timber guard booth in Birmingham in the 1920s
required: one silent broad-shouldered detective in a dark soaked overcoat and flat cap viewed from behind, no identifiable facial features
one weary mustached railway watchman in a period uniform coat and service cap looking down, his rifle safely slung across the shoulder
one illuminated old wooden guard booth, wet rail siding, cold canal water and a weathered timber lock gate in one continuous space
scenes.background: wet cobbles and railway rails curving past the guard booth, a canal-lock wheel and gate, soot-dark factories and smoking chimneys fading into industrial mist
scenes.light: warm lantern light on the watchman's downturned face and damp wooden booth, contrasting with cold blue-grey night fog on the canal and rails
scenes.npc: Jack is visible only from behind and cannot be mistaken for a new protagonist; the unnamed railway guard is seen in guarded three-quarter view, no additional participants
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: This character-specific confrontation occurs before the outcome of the player's decision. Neither a threat nor Jack's reference to Hale has necessarily gained the passage. Guard's averted gaze is hesitation, not a signed confession, a completed bribe, a physical attack or an earned witness statement. Jack's face remains unestablished and his chosen identity is preserved.
avoid: identifiable portrait of Jack or invented close-up face, additional civilian or Tommy appearing at the gate
the watchman pointing, firing or swinging the rifle at anyone, a fight or visible injury
an open unlocked gate, the detective already granted passage or a written guard confession
readable railway timetable, fabricated stamped evidence or an anachronistic modern security booth

scenes.focus: an observant man in a heavy rain-dark wool coat and tweed cap pauses on a steep narrow exterior iron staircase, his face concealed as he looks through an open freight-office window at shipping documents illuminated by a desk lamp
scenes.camera: vertical close-medium composition from behind the detective at stair level, a diagonal iron railing in the foreground and an open wooden-paned window leading the eye into the desk inside
scenes.location: the second-storey back wall of a late-night 1920s Birmingham private railway freight office beside a dark industrial siding
required: one man in a dark wool coat and flat cap with only the back of his head and hand on a wet iron railing visible
one open weathered wooden window above the narrow outdoor metal steps, with raindrops catching the light
one period office desk inside with a closed leather ledger, a single loose shipping paper, an inkstand and pigeonhole files
scenes.background: damp brickwork, black wrought-iron stairs, old railway wagons and wet tracks receding toward factory smokestacks under a smoky night sky
scenes.light: a warm desk lamp inside the office contrasts with cold blue-grey rain and a few distant amber railway lamps
scenes.npc: only the anonymous rear-view detective on the stairs; no other person is identifiable
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: Finn is using an opportunistic open window and exterior stairs to learn where a clean copy of the shipping ledger may be found. He is not shown stealing it, entering by force, opening any safe, acquiring the original document or proving which clerk forged it. The selected hero's approved facial appearance must not be invented.
avoid: Finn's identifiable face, a substituted player portrait, a uniformed second person at the window
bent safe door, picklock, broken window, forced entry or destroyed office furniture
shipping papers with readable false names, invented dates, forged signatures or a completed proof of guilt
an original ledger already in Finn's possession, a heroic getaway or discovered alarm

scenes.focus: a careful investigator in dark 1920s sleeves and black leather gloves holds the back of a worn archival freight-office document directly beneath an angled brass desk lamp, revealing faint shallow impressions from an earlier rubbed-out written entry, with a folding bellows camera ready on the desk to photograph the trace
scenes.camera: vertical close over-the-shoulder view of hands supporting the single sheet near the foreground, raking lamplight brushing across embossed paper and a period folding bellows camera on the right; only a fragment of the observer's coat enters the frame
scenes.location: a 1920s railway freight-office records room overlooking a rainy Birmingham industrial goods yard
required: one large pale sheet held delicately in two black leather-gloved hands with subtle indentation traces visible as non-readable relief under raking light
one brass articulated period desk lamp pointed obliquely along the surface of the document
one vintage folding bellows plate camera on the desk prepared for a careful photographic record beside a closed leather notebook and inkstand
scenes.background: a scuffed wooden records table, timber pigeonhole shelves, a rain-streaked multi-paned window looking over freight wagons and smoking brick factory chimneys
scenes.light: warm focused amber desk-lamp light revealing the paper texture against cool rainy industrial twilight through the window
scenes.npc: the selected investigator's shoulder and both hands only; no exposed face or identifiable clerk or other witness
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: The trace appears when the paper is viewed in side light and can later be photographed with documented provenance. This is the same physical document, not an independently corroborating second source. No fabricated readable confession, suspect, date, or clerk identity may be established by the art. The camera standing ready does not imply that the documentary photo has already been officially admitted as proof.
avoid: a legible accusation or invented signature on the paper or an invented identifiable witness
an identifiable heroine face, full portrait or newly established costume identity
two independent original documents or a second confession, solved corruption or arrested suspect
a completed passport, modern digital camera or modern office electronics

scenes.focus: a quiet negotiation across a carved wooden tea table between a reserved industrial proprietor with short carefully groomed silver beard and a dark-clad visiting gentleman seen only from behind; the proprietor has laid one unmarked folded inspector's report on the table without overtly handing it across
scenes.camera: intimate vertical medium interior view from just behind the visiting gentleman's left shoulder; the powerful older proprietor sits facing him, a document between porcelain teacups in the foreground, a heavy iron safe and rain-streaked factory windows beyond
scenes.location: a prosperous but soot-dark 1920s Birmingham factory manager's private office overlooking the industrial rail yard
required: one prosperous industrial proprietor of about fifty-five, broad-shouldered with carefully trimmed silver beard, heavy charcoal wool suit and dark waistcoat, seated with restrained expression
one visiting man in a dark elegant 1920s coat visible only from behind across an intimate tea table, his face and distinguishing features concealed
one unobtrusive folded inspector's report with indistinct printing resting beside an ornate china tea set on the polished wooden table
one heavy vintage iron safe in the background, framed by a wet multi-paned window and industrial smokestacks
scenes.background: wood-panelled office, carved leather chairs, old filing cabinets, framed factory painting, coal hearth and a misty railway-side factory yard beyond the glass
scenes.light: restrained warm fire and oil-lamp illumination grazes the report and the older man's silver beard while cool rain-dark daylight pours through the industrial office window
scenes.npc: one older silver-bearded factory proprietor and one visiting investigator seen strictly from behind; no distinguishable secretary or other person
scenes.knowledgeBoundary: This scene shows diplomatic access and a copy of an inspection document left on the manager's table, not a signed bargain, unearned independent evidence, a confirmed admission, or a completed retrieval. The cost of negotiations is resolved only in player actions and story state. The five selectable protagonists retain their independent identities.
avoid: an identifiable close-up face of the visitor or an invented permanent portrait of the selectable hero
a signed confession, guarantee of witness safety, contract, handcuffs or explicit victory gesture
readable charges, fabricated signatures, dates or evidence in the paper
an opened or emptied safe, stolen original records or a visible threat with a weapon
